# DeepSeek authored these cards in App Studio

English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

**Email Action DS** and **Meeting Planner DS** were generated by DeepSeek V4
Flash through the OnePlus 6's system agent. DeepSeek read the Card Studio skill
and App Design Flow references, wrote the source, rendered it in App Studio,
inspected native widgets, injected input, viewed screenshots and repaired defects.
Codex supplied requirements and review feedback, packaged the results and ran
independent checks. Codex did not edit the generated card, Splash or icon source.
The [original references](../README.md) retain their separate authorship.

| Presentation | Email | Meeting |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L0 glance | [glance.card](email-action/glance.card) + [data](email-action/glance.data.json) | [glance.card](meeting-planner/glance.card) + [data](meeting-planner/glance.data.json) |
| Expanded actionable card and full view | [main.splash](email-action/bundle/main.splash) | [main.splash](meeting-planner/bundle/main.splash) |
| Normal app manifest | [manifest.json](email-action/bundle/manifest.json) | [manifest.json](meeting-planner/bundle/manifest.json) |

Here “L0/L1/L2” describes glance, expanded card and full app presentation.
Only `.card` uses the Octoscript L0 language. The interactive views are Splash;
they do not prove support for an Octoscript language capability called L1 or L2.
The glance files are rendered artifacts, not a live notification/glance feed.

## Try the generated apps

On the prepared OnePlus 6, open **Hackathon Demos → App Hub → Email Action DS**
or **Meeting Planner DS**. Choose the entries ending in **DS**. The isolated
package is `dev.makepad.octosense.hackathon`; the existing Home is separate.
The [Android setup](../ANDROID.md) describes the test host and provider setup.

1. Email: **Ask app agent for a reply**. Allow the app's agent on first use,
   then retry. Inspect the **AI-written** draft, tap **Review reply**, verify
   the recipient and body, and **Confirm demo delivery**. Only a fake local
   outbox changes. **Undo this message's reply** keeps the draft.
2. Meeting: **Open full view**, ask which listed slot is free, allow the agent
   and retry. Return to the card, select a slot, **Review this slot**, then
   confirm the demo booking. **New 14:00 conflict** invalidates a stale proposal;
   choose 15:30 instead. **All busy** and **Reset demo** expose failure/recovery.
3. Without a provider, use **Insert offline sample reply** or **Suggest first
   free slot (offline)**. These are deterministic, explicitly labeled fallbacks.

Drag the right scrollbar to reach lower controls on the tested Android build.
The multiline reply editor scrolls long lines horizontally; **Review reply**
wraps the complete body. The floating shell control belongs to OctoSense.

For a desktop local run, complete [setup](../../../docs/QUICKSTART.md) and use:

```sh
tools/octo run examples/agentic-hackathon/deepseek-studio/email-action/bundle --hidden --detach --port 8481
tools/octo run examples/agentic-hackathon/deepseek-studio/meeting-planner/bundle --hidden --detach --port 8482
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8481/quit
curl --fail http://127.0.0.1:8482/quit
```

Omit `--hidden` for a visible window. `card-host` has no agent service, so its
AI buttons exercise the explicit unavailable path. Real agent replies require
an OctoSense shell, a configured provider and per-app consent.

## Reproduce the authoring loop

Give the authoring agent the [briefs and defect reports](validation/operator-briefs/BRIEF.md),
the [Card Studio skill](https://github.com/OctoSense-org/OctoSense-App-Hub/blob/927f2fe0c06b620f47f2f25befd0b2cb0bafe244/skills/card-studio/SKILL.md),
[Script App Flow](../../../flows/script-app/FLOW.md),
[Script API](../../../docs/SCRIPT-API.md), and
[model validation rules](../../../docs/MODEL-VALIDATION.md).

On this phone the skill's render/review loop uses the native `studio.render`
tool. Interactive previews use `studio.bundle_check`, `studio.open`,
`studio.inspect`, `studio.input`, `view_image` and `studio.close`. The model
calls these tools itself; the operator's later ADB taps are separate validation.
The skill's desktop `card-studio` command is not an Android executable.

The tested Studio host admits **storage-only** previews. Each example retains
its model-authored `preview-manifest.json`; normal `bundle/manifest.json` adds
the model-authored app-agent declaration and turn capabilities. Both paths use
the same `main.splash` bytes. A preview cannot establish provider or consent
coverage. Install a signed copy in a private catalog to validate those paths.

Keep feedback concrete: name the failed input, observed storage/UI result and
required invariant. DeepSeek repaired invented dataset fields, missing UTC,
invalid confirmation after edits, ineffective object-key deletion, duplicate
meeting bookings, inaccessible long views and empty layout regions. After each
repair, rerun the relevant native behavior and review the actual image. Do not
treat the model's self-review or a zero-error render as functional proof.

## Trace and verify

`load → save → ask_agent/ask_question → review → confirm → undo` is the useful
reading order. `save` places fixtures and state under `accounts/device/`, the
workspace the app peer can read. Email passes the selected fictional message
to its draft prompt. Calendar points the peer to `calendar.json` and `state.json`.
`octos.turn.start` returns a text proposal; local code checks and writes a
reviewed action. The model has no real send or booking tool, and the bundle
contains no provider credential.

```sh
python3 -B examples/agentic-hackathon/deepseek-studio/verify_native.py
tools/octo check examples/agentic-hackathon/deepseek-studio/email-action/bundle
tools/octo check examples/agentic-hackathon/deepseek-studio/meeting-planner/bundle
```

The [validation record](validation/README.md) separates model-run Studio checks,
33 independent desktop assertions and phone integration. It includes exact
source hashes and a sanitized tool record. The per-app `DESIGN.md` and `REVIEW.md`
are raw model notes from intermediate rounds, retained as provenance; they
are not the final operator acceptance report.

These remain hackathon references over fake data. Cross-app delegation,
background notifications, production publishing and delivery to real accounts
are outside this run. The listing's publisher/privacy placeholders must be
replaced by the actual publisher before a public submission.
